h: Your Guide to a Quieter Norfolk Wildlife Day
p: If the Golden Mile has worn everyone out, Thrigby is a lovely way to slow the pace. The grounds feel like a mature country garden as much as a zoo, with big trees, winding paths and plenty of shade on a hot day. Little ones can play spot-the-animal around every corner, while grown-ups enjoy the peace and quiet compared with the seafront.

Try to time your visit around the tigers' active spells. Big cats can spend a lot of the day snoozing, so asking staff when they're most likely to be up and about can make all the difference. The swamp house is a winner on cooler days, and its crocodiles are guaranteed to get a reaction from the kids.

Practical tips: there's parking on site, which makes it easy to slot into a car-based holiday, and it's a short drive from most of the caravan parks and holiday villages around Great Yarmouth, Caister and Hemsby. Take a picnic if you fancy, and comfy shoes for the paths.

There's plenty to combine with it in this corner of Norfolk. Caister-on-Sea, just down the road, has a wide, sandy beach and an independent lifeboat station with a proud history, while the ruins of Caister Castle sit just inland. A bit further south, Burgh Castle has the impressive remains of a Roman fort overlooking Breydon Water, with big skies and good walking. And of course, the Norfolk Broads are all around you, so hiring a day boat for a gentle potter along the rivers and waterways is a brilliant way to finish off a holiday.
